packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-09 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or
reading of this packet. I opened only the brief, PROMPT.md and the image files
in the packet directory (the directory listing showed a packet.json, which I did
not open).

LAYOUT SURVEY (written from image-001, overview of face A)

image-001: overview of one face, with a cm ruler below (0-30 cm). Parchment
strip, landscape, c. 28 x 16 cm. Two blocks of text, each c. 9 cm wide, left
block from c. 4.5 to 13.5 cm, right block from c. 15 to 24 cm, separated by a
c. 1.5-2 cm gap in which sits a small round library stamp (ink, circular, with
a lion? device) at c. 13.5 cm. A vertical fold/crease runs near the stamp. I
cannot tell from the overview whether the two blocks are two columns of one
page or the facing pages of a bifolium cut down; the gap is narrow, which leans
toward two columns or a tight gutter -- tentative.
Each block shows c. 22 lines; the top line of each block is cut through at the
upper edge (text lost above). Below the text there is c. 6 cm of blank lower
margin. At the far left, a vertical strip c. 2 cm wide, darker, with a pinhole/
sewing holes -- looks like a binding strip/turn-in (observation; function
tentative). At the right, beyond the right block, a large blank area with later
pen trials/flourishes and a later note reading roughly "...egond?" and "1809"
(or "1899"?) in brown ink, partly faded.
Script: a Gothic bookhand (textualis/hybrida-like, fairly upright, with
looped ascenders on some letters), brown-black ink, single size; no rubrics or
enlarged initials visible on this face except some letters touched in red? (a
faint red mark near left block line 4). Language visibly vernacular (Dutch-
looking: "vande welke", "dat es", "daer", "zulle") with embedded Latin
quotations ("Si in viridi ligno hoc faciunt in arido quid fiet", "oportuit
xpm pati", "Ne dixeris peccaui"), each followed by "Dat es" introducing a
vernacular rendering. Chapter references "int xxiij capitle va(n) S(int) luuc".
Some strike-through deletions visible (left block line 8 start, line 20).
No interlinear or marginal glosses seen on the overview.
Tiles: image-002..005 are presumably native-resolution tiles of this face;
image-006 presumably the overview of the other face; image-007..010 its tiles.
To be confirmed as each is opened.

SUMMARY OF COVERAGE AND LIMITATIONS

Selected / read: all four text blocks (2 per face), every surviving line,
at native resolution: face A left block (002.01-003.11, 22 lines), face A
right block (004.01-005.11, 22 lines), face B left block (007.01-008.11,
22 lines), face B right block (009.01-010.11, 22 lines). All 10 images
opened; none blank.
Unread: the top line of each block is cut at the upper edge (only letter
feet survive; partly read for face A left and face B left and right);
text above that is lost. Individual words left uncertain or [illegible] are
marked in place (abrasion, stains, blot in face A right line 10, crease in
face B right line 9).
Structure (observation): Dutch-looking vernacular prose with embedded Latin
quotations (face A: "Si in viridi ligno hoc faciunt in arido quid fiet",
"Nonne hec oportuit xpm pati", "Ne dixeris peccaui"), each followed by
"Dat es" + vernacular rendering; chapter references ("int xxiij capitle
van Sint luuc", "int xxiiij(te) capitle van Sint luuc", "int v° ca ...
ecti"); a cited name "sextus pitag?or?ius" on face B. Quotations are written
in the same hand and size as the vernacular, not set off by colour or
underlining.
Unresolved: whether each face carries two columns of one page or two pages
of a bifolium; the order of the four blocks; the citation formula in

Script conventions used: r-rotunda after o/round letters read as r
(e.g. "droeghe", "voor"); horizontal stroke over final vowel expanded as
(n); "en" with stroke as en(de); "hee" with stroke as h(er)e; "ihus"/"ihu"/
"ihm" with stroke as ih(esu)s etc.; z-like mark after -ich as (eit).
Later additions (not text): stamp "BIBLIOTHECA GANDAVENSIS" (face A gap);
brown ink pen trials and "...egond?" / "1809?" at right of face A; pencil
note in the lower margin of face B ("gekocht op ...", a date) -- I record
these as observations only, not as provenance inference.
Did anything beyond the rules: no. No crops made. Did not stop on the image
limit.
